speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you describe the nature of your vertigo—is it a sensation that the room is spinning around you, or do you feel like you are losing your balance and might fall? Also, did this episode start suddenly while you were resting or moving your head?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any associated hearing loss, ringing in the ears, or a feeling of fullness in one ear? Also, do you have a history of migraines or vascular risk factors like hypertension or diabetes?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Sudden-onset sensation of the room spinning. I also have Nausea, Vomiting, Dizziness.

speaker: Doctor
text: Did the vertigo episode last less than a minute, or did it persist for several minutes to hours? Also, does changing your head position, such as rolling over in bed or looking up, consistently trigger these spinning sensations?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: The patient is otherwise healthy with only a history of eczema. No prior episodes of similar nature. Social history: No significant social history provided.

The symptoms strongly suggest Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV), so I need to confirm the presence of nystagmus triggered by head position changes.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Positive, inducing nystagmus and reproducing patient’s symptoms of vertigo when head is turned to the left and laid back.

speaker: Doctor
text: The Dix-Hallpike maneuver is positive on the left side, which confirms the diagnosis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV)
